# ARC

1. On an autumn afternoon on the coral reef, where leaves from the shore drift down through the water, four-year-old Léa swims in front of her family holding a strand of seaweed in which her brother Jules has tied grandfather Henri's thank-you, a knot that speaks Henri's words when Salomé unties it, and she wants to put it into the hands of Salomé, the mermaid who rings her shell bell before every storm and has never heard merci, before the bell rings at dusk tonight, which is why the family has come down to the reef.
2. Henri, whose boat passed the rocks safely in the last storm because of Salomé's bell and who spoke the thank-you for Jules to knot, knows from sailing over the reef that the other way into the shoal takes until after dark, so he tells everyone to take the short way under the coral arch, with Marc and Élodie swimming behind Léa.
3. Under the arch a moray eel comes out of the shadow, opens her jaws wide and blocks the way, and Léa swims up to the arch and calls Salomé with all her voice.
4. Salomé answers from the shoal, names the eel Mina and asks her to let the child through, but Mina keeps the way shut, and Salomé cannot leave her bell rock before the bell rings at the last light.
5. Élodie asks Mina what she wants, and Mina answers that swimmers in a hurry broke a branch off the foot of the arch, that she has no hands to set it back in its notch, and that no one passes until it is set.
6. Marc grabs the branch and pushes it at the notch in a rush, Mina's jaws snap shut an inch from his fingers, and he pulls back.
7. Jules tries next, slowly, but his fingers are too big for the narrow notch, the light turns grey, and Léa, whose hand is the only one that fits, hides her face against Élodie's side.
8. Léa looks again, sees that Mina's jaws open and close slowly and snap only at fast hands, and decides to go; Jules ties the seaweed around her wrist so that both her hands are free, and Marc tells her to move slowly and keep her fingers away from the jaws.
9. Léa swims slowly past the open jaws, turns the branch into the notch with her small hand, and it holds, so Mina closes her jaws, slides aside, says merci to Léa, and lets the family pass under the arch one by one.
10. At the bell rock Léa gives Salomé the seaweed, Salomé unties the knot and hears Henri's voice say merci, and she ties the seaweed to the bell rope, says merci to Léa, and lets her pull the rope with her, so that the bell rings at the last light and Léa laughs.
